label: 01 | Prepare an admin account, repository installation rights, and a dedicated review identity. Existing tenant walkthrough; no new grants are made.
02 | Create API token with scopes > choose Bitbucket > set expiry > select every required scope. Omit repository write for advisory-only use.
03 | Sign in with Bitbucket Cloud as the workspace admin, approve OAuth, select the workspace, then save the review-account token privately.
04 | Connected repositories: filter the intended repositories, select them, and Install. All six shown here are already installed.
05 | Account > Bitbucket user: enter the review-account email and token, then Save. This is an unsaved example; existing credentials stay in place.
06 | Bitbucket Repository settings > Workflow > Webhooks: verify the CodeRabbit endpoint, Active status, TLS verification, and PR event triggers.
07 | Connections > Add connection > Jira: give it a name, choose the Jira Cloud Review connection, and use Forge for native issue context.
07 | For a new site: Connect with Forge > install the app in Jira > enter the 15-minute secret > Complete Setup > refresh CodeRabbit status. Existing site shown next.
08 | Scopes control which repositories can use a connection. The Base Scope has zero connections; CSAA demo context covers six repositories.
09 | Add the chosen .coderabbit.yaml at the repository root. Adapt repository links, approved Jira project keys, guidelines, and review triggers before saving.
09 | This evaluation profile uses manual reviews and warning-mode checks. For automatic PR reviews, approve and enable auto_review for the customer pilot.
10 | Verify a real PR: link the approved Jira issue, inspect resolved settings, and confirm the review plus linked-issue and scope checks.
10 | Readiness evidence: PR 14 passes linked-issue, change-scope and approved-context checks. Application CI is a separate signal.
11 | For manual reviews, type @coderabbitai full review and submit when ready. This recording leaves the request as an unsent draft.
12 | Before handoff, verify seats and plan access, non-draft PR eligibility, target branches, token expiry, webhook delivery, and expected review triggers.
